items.title: 68163_Tom Whaley oral history interview
items.q: Dr.Towle, right at 72nd Street and Park Avenue. So he couldn't do nothing. None of these doctors could do anything for me

ctx.x: Was this doctor, downtown or up in Harlem.

Dr.Towle, right at 72nd Street and Park Avenue. So he couldn't do nothing. None of these doctors could do anything for me, because I went up there at the Medical Center and that doctor up there, he was giving me drops but they didn't seem to work and I had glasses and Radio City, there, I used to go in that opticians there and they used to examine my eyes and give me glasses.

If you can just think of some kind of little anecdotes or some of your old associations with Duke, I'm sure people would like to know because you all were so close. You told me before that Duke always carried a pencil with him and he would go around and mark different things. Can you tell me something about that.
